title: deploy-day-rapid-todo
content:
Purpose:
Quick, personal, readable run-through for today’s deploy/cutover. Not the official runbook — this is my rapid checklist and immediate callouts to keep in my head while I drive the push. To be used alongside the canonical runbook (linked above).

High level:
- Target window: 09:00–11:00 PT (customer-facing low traffic window).
- Release: serving-runtime v1.9.2 -> v1.10.0 (major runtime perf kernels + batching changes).
- Hotfix backports included: rleng/2391 (kv-cache fix), rleng/2378 (quant conv table).

Pre-cutover (T-90 to T-5 minutes):
- [ ] Confirm all preflight CI green (smoke + canary tests). Command: ./ci/run_smoke.sh --tag v1.10.0 
- [ ] Confirm Dedicated pool health (grafana: /d/pool-health) — ping @sre on Slack if any amber.
- [ ] Validate DB migration no-op: run migration dry-run: scripts/db_migrate_check.sh --dry-run
- [ ] Ensure RBAC / secrets are present in staging and prod K8s: kubectl -n prod get secrets serving-keys -o yaml | grep lastUpdated
- [ ] Finalize release notes and send one-line to #releases channel: "Rolling v1.10.0 -> prod 09:00 PT. Expected <2% transient 5xx during rollout; automatic fallback enabled."

Cutover quick sequence (my shorthand):
1) Lock the rollout: set rollout-mode=manual in console (prevent auto-canary expansion)
2) Deploy canary to 3 pods on us-west-2 (route 5% traffic). Wait 5m.
3) Run perf soak script: tools/perf_soak.py --target=canary --requests=5000 --p95-threshold=200ms
4) If perf OK, increment to 25% for 10m. Check latency and errors.
5) If everything green, full rollout via console -> schedule gradual expansion.
6) Monitor fallback triggers: fallback to v1.9.2 if error rate > 1% for 10m.

Immediate post-deploy checks (first 30m):
- [ ] Check token-level cost metrics for spikes: Console -> Billing -> Token-cost per-route (look for large jump on /chat-stream).
- [ ] Run smoke end-to-end: scripts/e2e_check.sh --env=prod --suite=chat,embeddings
- [ ] Validate KV cache hitrate: grafana panel "kv_cache_hitrate" (should not drop >5% from baseline).
- [ ] Confirm telemetry ingestion (prod-telemetry) is functioning: kubectl logs telemetry-processor | tail -n 200 | grep "ingest_ok"
- [ ] Verify canary rollback path: run simulate-failure.sh against canary and ensure auto-fallback fires (dry-run flag available).

Backports & patches to watch (personal notes):
- rleng/2391: kv-cache crash on mid-length seqs — backported to stable branch and included in release. Confirm PR merged to both branches.
- rleng/2378: quant conv table generation discrepancy — merged but re-run unit tests for quant path on a small instance (g4dn.xlarge).
- Edge case: open issue RLENG-2419 flagged by Leah — memory leak under repeated batching. Mitigation: temporary cap batch size at 32 if seen in prod.

Comms / stakeholders (who I ping):
- @Leah Kim (SRE lead) — watch grafana for mem/cpu and errors.
- @Priya Rao (Serving runtime) — on call for any kernel-related perf regressions.
- @CS Ops (#cs-ops) — heads up: potential minor transient errors affecting 0.1% of customers.
- Exec note: send a short update to #exec-updates if rollout completes without incident.

Escalation matrix (fast reference):
- Sev2 perf regression (p95 > 2x baseline): @Leah Kim -> @SRE Manager (pager: +1-628-555-0142) -> execs.
- Sev1 outage (route 503/5xx > 5%): Immediate rollback and page SRE team via #pagerduty, call the oncall.

Short commands I’ll run (copy/paste):
- CI smoke: ./ci/run_smoke.sh --tag v1.10.0 || echo "SMOKE FAILED" && exit 1
- Perf soak (canary): python3 tools/perf_soak.py --target=canary --rps=50 --duration=300
- Check pods: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide
- Force rollback: ./scripts/rollout_control.sh --env=prod --action=rollback --to-tag=v1.9.2 --reason="auto-trigger"

Post-cutover watchlist (hours 1–6):
- Errors: aggregate 5xx and 4xx — expect small transient bumps but should settle within 15–30m.
- Latency: track p50/p95/p99 and compare to baseline from last week.
- Memory: watch for slow upward drift — if the 95th percentile of pod memory climbs >10% over baseline for two consecutive 10m windows, scale down rollout and investigate.
- Billing: token cost per-route should remain within margin; unusually high token counts may indicate prompt loop bug.

Personal reminders / TODOs while I’m running this:
- [ ] Keep Slack thread tidy: pin the perf soak results and main graph image.
- [ ] If fallback triggers, quickly assemble timeline and file an incident doc (use template in Confluence).
- [ ] After 2 hours, do a short retrospective note in this doc: what went well, what surprised, action items.

Odd-ball checks (I always forget these until too late):
- CDN invalidation for statics (if rollout included UI change): aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id XXX --paths "/static/*"
- Verify alerting rules fired correctly: /alerting -> check RLENG-alerts -> evaluate rule history for last 60m

End-of-day wrap:
- [ ] Short debrief ping to #releases with TL;DR and link to incident doc if any.
- [ ] Push action items to playlist: link -> Confluence "Cutover follow-ups" and assign owners.

Notes to self: keep calm, small failures are expected. Use the rollback path early if multiple indicators point bad. Prioritize customer-facing service continuity over feature completeness.
